tier1.text: The sarcoplasmic reticulum stores calcium that a muscle cell needs to contract. The sarcoplasmic reticulum is a fine network of membranes that runs all through the cell. An electrical signal makes the sarcoplasmic reticulum release calcium, which starts the contraction. Pumps then move the calcium back into storage, so the cell relaxes.

sentences.text: The sarcoplasmic reticulum stores calcium that a muscle cell needs to contract.

quotes.quote: In muscle cells, a specialized SER, the sarcoplasmic reticulum, is responsible for storing calcium ions that are needed to trigger the muscle cells' coordinated contractions.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The sarcoplasmic reticulum is a fine network of membranes that runs all through the cell.

quotes.quote: A fine reticular network of membrane-limited elements that pervades the sarcoplasm of a muscle cell

sentences.text: An electrical signal makes the sarcoplasmic reticulum release calcium, which starts the contraction.

quotes.quote: triggering an action potential that spreads to the rest of the membrane which will depolarize, including the T-tubules. This triggers the release of calcium ions (Ca++) from storage in the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR). The Ca++ then initiates contraction
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Pumps then move the calcium back into storage, so the cell relaxes.

quotes.quote: ATP-driven pumps will move Ca++ out of the sarcoplasm back into the SR. This results in the “reshielding” of the actin-binding sites on the thin filaments. Without the ability to form cross-bridges between the thin and thick filaments, the muscle fiber loses its tension and relaxes.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
